commitResults.messageTitle: Edit command: Reject phone or email used by others
commitResults.messageBody:
Editing a contact can give it the phone number or email of another
contact. Phone numbers and emails are meant to identify one contact
each, so such an edit creates two records for what may be the same
person.

Let's reject the whole edit when the new phone number or email
already belongs to another contact, naming that contact, as
specified in UC04 (extension 2c). Emails are compared case-
insensitively, since letter case does not change the address.

Only edited fields are checked, so contacts whose existing details
already clash can still have their other fields edited.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add log command to record interactions with a contact
commitResults.messageBody:
Astra stores who a contact is, but not what was discussed with them,
which is the context a networker needs before meeting someone again
(UC10).

Let's let the user record dated interactions:
  log INDEX|NAME [d/DATE] nt/NOTE
* the date defaults to today and cannot be in the future
* the history is kept in date order, so a late entry is placed where
  it belongs
* logging the same note on the same date twice is rejected
* the updated history is shown after logging, and in view

The history is saved with each contact. Files written before this
change have no interactions field and load with an empty history.
Editing a contact carries the history over unchanged.

Person keeps its existing constructors; the history is attached with
withInteractions(), to avoid clashing with other open changes to
Person.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Xt8WZiTKRufrmH5H1szLZL

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find /notes to search interaction notes
commitResults.messageBody:
The notes recorded with log can only be read one contact at a time,
so the user cannot find who they discussed a topic with (UC08).

Let's add "find /notes KEYWORDS", which lists contacts with a note
containing any of the keywords, ignoring case, and shows the matching
notes with their dates under each contact. Long notes are shortened
to the part around the match.

Any keyword may match, since a search the user half-remembers is more
useful than one that needs every word. As the User Guide describes
for find, the displayed list is left as it was when nothing matches.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add alias command to define command shortcuts
commitResults.messageBody:
Users who network a lot repeat the same long commands, such as
find /email, many times a day. Typing them in full is slow.

Let users save a one-word shortcut for a command (UC27):
alias fe find /email makes fe ADDRESS run find /email ADDRESS.
alias lists shortcuts, alias /replace replaces one and
alias /remove removes one.

A shortcut cannot reuse a built-in command word, and must expand to
a built-in command other than alias. This keeps expansion to a
single step, so shortcuts can never loop. Defining a shortcut that
already exists shows its current expansion and changes nothing,
instead of overwriting it silently.

Shortcuts are stored in UserPrefs and written to preferences.json
as soon as they change, rather than only when the app closes, so
they are not lost if the app is killed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Xt8WZiTKRufrmH5H1szLZL

commitResults.messageTitle: Add unlog command to remove a logged interaction
commitResults.messageBody:
An interaction logged with the wrong date, note or person could not
be fixed, because log only adds entries. The only way out was editing
the data file by hand.

Add unlog INDEX|NAME i/ENTRY, where ENTRY is the interaction's number
in the history shown by view and log. The person is found the same
way as log. Astra shows what was removed and the remaining history,
renumbered, so the user can check the result straight away.

An entry number past the end of the history, or a person with no
interactions, is rejected and nothing changes.

commitResults.messageBody:

commitResults.messageTitle: Add editlog command to correct logged interactions
commitResults.messageBody:

unlog followed by log, which needs a confirmation, retyping the part
that was right, and loses the entry if the second command fails.

editlog INDEX|NAME i/ENTRY [d/DATE] [nt/NOTE] replaces one entry in
place. Dates follow the same rules as log (the past-date check is
shared), the history stays in date order, and the result reports the
entry's new number. Edits that change nothing or would duplicate
another entry are rejected.

commitResults.messageTitle: Rework Person model for Astra's contact fields
commitResults.messageBody:
AB3's person carried a name, phone, email and address. Astra captures
people met at networking events, where the useful details are who someone
works for and what they do, and where an address is never collected.

Replace the address with a company, a role and a LinkedIn profile, and make
every field other than the name optional: a contact is often captured with
only a name and whatever was exchanged before the conversation moved on, so
requiring a phone and an email would make the app unusable for its own
purpose. Optional fields are nullable internally and exposed as Optional,
so callers cannot read an absent value by accident.

Identity is unchanged for now: two persons are still duplicates when their
names match. Keying on the contact number or email instead, and allowing
several values per field, are both later changes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Hold contact fields to the rules the DG specifies
commitResults.messageBody:
Three gaps between the model and our own Developer Guide:

Normalisation. The glossary defines a display value as the normalised
spelling that Astra stores and shows, with outer spaces trimmed and
repeated spaces collapsed. Only the parsers trimmed, so "John  Doe" was
stored with two spaces and a value loaded straight from the save file was
never tidied at all. Add StringUtil#normalise and apply it in every field's
constructor, so a value is normalised wherever it enters the model.

Names. NFR 9 requires names containing non-English letters, but the
validation regex used the ASCII-only \p{Alnum}, so "Jose Garcia" was
rejected. Match Unicode letters and numbers instead, and allow the hyphens,
apostrophes and full stops that ordinary names contain.

Phone numbers. The glossary describes digits with optional balanced
parentheses and at least three digits; the regex accepted bare digits only,
so "+65 9312 1534" was rejected. Accept spaces, hyphens, a leading plus and
balanced parentheses, while still requiring three digits and rejecting
anything else. Parentheses are checked by counting depth rather than by
regex, so an unbalanced "(65 9312" is caught.

Two existing assertions change meaning as a result: an email with outer
spaces and a name with trailing spaces are now normalised rather than
rejected, which is what the glossary asks for and what the parsers already
did before validating.

Astra lets the user name a contact instead of giving its index when
finding and editing one, so delete should accept a name too: deleting by
index alone means having to find someone before you can remove them, even
when you already know exactly who you want gone.

The matching rule is find's, not a new one. Name resolution lived as
private methods inside EditCommand, and copying it into DeleteCommand
would have given Astra two answers to what naming a contact means --
exactly the inconsistency that put the earlier draft of this feature on
hold. Instead, PersonNameResolver now owns that single answer and both
commands go through it, so the rule cannot drift as more commands gain
the ability. Its Outcome is a sealed type of Unique or Several, which
makes the ambiguous case a value rather than an error and leaves no
Person for a command to reach for until the user has narrowed it down.

Resolving a name searches every contact rather than the displayed list,
so naming someone reaches them even while a find filter hides them, and
the full list is restored once the deletion is done. Deleting by index
still works on the list the user is looking at and leaves that view
alone.

Deciding whether the user typed an index or a name is shared the same
way, as ParserUtil#isIndexInput, so no input can be read as an index by
one command and as a name by another.

delete on an empty address book now reports that there is nothing to
delete, rather than complaining about an invalid index.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make the README and DG describe the MVP we actually ship
commitResults.messageBody:
Three documents claimed more than v1.3 delivers. Each claim was checked
against the code rather than reworded from the old text.

README feature list:

- "multiple companies, roles, numbers and emails per person" - Person
  holds one Company, Role, Phone, Email and Linkedin, each optional, and
  has done since the v1.2 model rework.
- "delete contacts by email, phone number or name, after confirmation" -
  delete takes an index or a name, and there is no confirmation prompt.
- "lets you keep, replace or merge the records" - there is no merge flow.
  add refuses a second contact with the same name; edit refuses a phone
  number or email already saved for another contact. add does not check
  for a duplicate number or email at all, so the README no longer implies
  it does.

DG glossary: the Contact definition said "one or more companies, roles,
contact numbers and emails", the same multi-valued claim as the README.

DG user stories: "clear all contacts after confirming" was a `* * *`
must-have, so the MVP failed a must-have story on paper even though the
promptless clear was a deliberate decision. Split into a must-have
"clear all contacts", which ships, and a `* *` "be asked to confirm
before contacts are deleted or cleared", which does not.

Everything removed is recorded under "Planned for after the MVP" in the
README rather than deleted, so the requirements survive the trim. Two
gaps surfaced while checking and are listed there as future work: add
does not reject a duplicate phone number or email the way edit does, and
Name equality is case-sensitive, so "alice pauline" and "Alice Pauline"
are currently two different contacts.

Docs only. .github/run-checks.sh reports no new warnings; the seven
pre-existing trailing-whitespace warnings in the DG are untouched except
on the glossary line, which this commit rewrites anyway.

Names are also compared case-sensitively, so "Test" and "test" are
stored as two contacts even though every name lookup ignores case
(#234).

without regard to letter case when deciding whether two contacts are
the same person.

Contacts with the same name but different emails remain allowed, so

commitResults.messageTitle: Report phone and email clashes before duplicates
commitResults.messageBody:
When an edit gives a contact the email of another contact with the same
name, EditCommand reports "This person already exists in the contact
file." The user changed only the email, so the message points at the
wrong field (#236).

The general duplicate check runs before the phone and email checks, so
it hides their more specific messages.

Run the phone and email checks first, both before the preview and on
confirmation. The edit is then rejected with the clashing value and the
contact that already has it. The general duplicate message remains for
the case where no phone or email clashes.

Fixes #236

commitResults.messageTitle: Name mistyped prefixes in parse errors
commitResults.messageBody:
A mistyped prefix, such as "ph/" instead of "p/", is not recognized by
the tokenizer, so it stays inside the value of the previous field.
"add n/John ph/123" then reports that the name is invalid, which sends
the user looking for a problem in the name instead of the prefix
(#238).

Names, phone numbers, emails and tags can never contain a slash. When
one of these values is invalid and contains a word ending in a slash,
report that word as an unrecognized prefix instead of the field's
constraints. Values that are invalid for other reasons keep their
existing messages.

Fixes #238

no test calls it directly. Its null branch is never exercised, which
leaves the new line only partly covered and fails the codecov/patch
